candidates.name: Chromoblastomycosis
support_spans: asymptomatic erythematous scaly plaques over the face and proximal extremities
pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia, parakeratosis, dense dermal infiltrate of histiocytes, foamy histiocytes, neutrophils, and multinucleate giant cells along with pigmented hyphae
candidates.why: The patient's presentation of erythematous scaly plaques with central scarring and the histopathological findings are consistent with Chromoblastomycosis.

candidates.name: Wegener's granulomatosis
support_spans: involvement of the upper respiratory tract, causing palatal perforation and stridor
saddle nose deformity, perforation of the hard palate
contradict_spans: no history of preceding trauma, fever, malaise, joint pain, cough, epistaxis, hemoptysis, or hematuria
candidates.why: The patient's upper respiratory tract involvement and saddle nose deformity are consistent with Wegener's granulomatosis, but the lack of other systemic symptoms and negative serologic tests make it less likely.

candidates.name: Phaeohyphomycosis
support_spans: infiltrate of foamy histiocytes and pigmented yeasts without multiaxial septation (Fontana-Masson)
fungal skin culture: black yeastlike colonies characteristic of Exophiala spinifera species
candidates.why: The patient's skin biopsy and fungal culture results are consistent with Phaeohyphomycosis, a fungal infection caused by Exophiala spinifera.
